{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-al-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"d109740231546379774bc9ed4f4feb82ad94804cd43fbed9a2e5d19c9ac27264","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-al-class-d:lineage:10","source_registry_sha256":"ea8231e949706ecda9f2a398d6eaf9ab30e224ac7defb0e6291b764b84ed0d95","source_liveness_sha256":"e524456f547beacfeca0647b02ef401523e58aa5b835501e7cbdd821b6546315"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Cancellation, revocation, suspension and the point system","heading":"C — Cancellation, revocation, suspension and the point system","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Cancellation, revocation, suspension and the point system

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A19
On top of whatever the court imposes, a conviction for breaking a traffic law can cost you your license through cancellation, revocation, suspension or disqualification. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A19
Getting relicensed after a cancellation, suspension, revocation or disqualification requires a reinstatement fee of at least $100 plus any other state-law requirements. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A19
Failing to surrender your license within the allowed time after it is canceled, revoked or suspended adds a $50 fee. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A19
Reinstatement after a drug-related conviction costs an extra $25, and reinstating after a suspension for unpaid child support costs an extra $50. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A19
The ALEA Director may cancel a license on finding the holder was not entitled to it, and missing or false application information or application fraud is also grounds for cancellation. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A19
Once a revocation period ends, the driver may apply for a new license but must take and pass the complete examinations again. [A19]
Why it matters: revocation ends the license, so unlike a suspension it is not simply reinstated afterward.
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A19
The Director must revoke a license after a conviction for manslaughter or homicide caused by operating a motor vehicle, or for using a motor vehicle to commit a felony. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A19
Revocation is also mandatory on a second or later conviction for driving or being in actual physical control of a vehicle under the influence of alcohol, or for driving as a habitual user of, or while too impaired by, a controlled substance to drive safely. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A19
Failing to stop, give aid, or identify yourself after a crash that kills or injures another person is a mandatory revocation offense. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A19
Perjury or a false sworn statement to the Director about license or vehicle laws, three reckless driving convictions within 12 months, and unauthorized use of someone else's vehicle all require revocation. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A20
A license may be suspended after certain convictions or a finding of incompetence to drive, and it is reinstated afterward unless it expired meanwhile or the suspension requirements were not all met. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A20
Suspension grounds include serious moving-violation convictions frequent enough to show disrespect for traffic laws, a record of habitually reckless or negligent driving, and incompetence to drive. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A20
Allowing unlawful or fraudulent use of your license, mutilating it, or committing an offense in another state that would be grounds here can also lead to suspension. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A20
Convictions for fleeing or trying to elude a police officer or for racing on highways can bring suspension, as can failing to answer a traffic summons on time or failing to pay. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A20
Drivers aged 15 through 18 who withdraw from school before graduating, under certain conditions, can have the license suspended. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A20
Failing to keep SR-22 insurance when it is required, unpaid child support, and medical reasons are further grounds for suspension. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A20
The suspension list includes having 4 or more points on the driving record, or 2 or more moving violations while holding a Graduated Driver License. [A20]
Why it matters: this list line uses a different count from the point-suspension schedule, so each threshold must be learned in its own context.
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A20
A first-offense DUI or drug offense, for a juvenile or an adult, is listed as grounds for suspension. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A20
Alabama's point system suspends licenses on uniform grounds, and points are charged for listed offenses whether they happen in Alabama or elsewhere. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A20
A conviction on a charge involving drinking alcohol and driving that did not require mandatory revocation carries 6 points. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A21
Reckless driving or reckless endangerment with a motor vehicle carries 6 points, and an Admin Per Se violation also carries 6 points. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A21
Failing to yield the right of way and passing a stopped school bus each carry 5 points. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A21
Driving on the wrong side of the road or passing illegally carries 4 points, and following too closely carries 3 points. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A21
Speeding 1 to 25 mph over the limit carries 2 points, but speeding 26 mph or more over the limit carries 5 points. [A21]
Why it matters: crossing the twenty-six mph line more than doubles the points for the same kind of ticket.
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A21
Failing to obey construction or maintenance zone markers carries 3 points. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A21
Inability to control the vehicle, an improper lane violation, drinking alcohol while operating a vehicle, improper motorcycle operation, and an emergency vehicle violation each carry 2 points. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A21
Failing to signal or using the wrong turn signal, making an improper turn, coasting, and unsafe operation each carry 2 points. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A21
Within a 2-year period, 12 to 14 points bring a 60-day suspension, 15 to 17 points bring 90 days, and 18 to 20 points bring 120 days. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A21
Within a 2-year period, 21 to 23 points bring a 180-day suspension, and 24 or more points bring 365 days. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A21
After receiving a suspension notice, a driver may ask for a pre-suspension or administrative hearing before an ALEA agent in the home county. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A21
An administrative hearing can be requested in writing to Driver License Services or online. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0021]

Glossary: cancellation — voiding a license the holder was never entitled to [A19]. Revocation — ending a license, after which a new one requires the complete examinations [A19]. Suspension — a withdrawal for a set period after which the license is reinstated if it has not expired and all requirements are met [A20]. Point system — Alabama's uniform method of charging points per offense toward suspension [A20].
Memory aid: cancel means it should never have been issued, revoke means start over, suspend means wait it out [A19].
